{"baseRefName":"main","body":"`DeclaredCaps` documents the capabilities that agents can have without declaring them through `DeclaredCapabilities`. That list had fallen out of date more than once, and some callers skipped the `As*` helpers entirely by type-asserting agents directly, which also skipped the declaration check.\n\nThis PR makes the list and the helpers enforceable, so reviewers no longer have to keep them in sync by hand.\n\n## What changed\n\nEvery package-level `As*` capability helper now resolves through one of three standard functions:\n\n- `declaredCapability`: a `CapabilityDeclarer` must implement the interface and declare the matching `DeclaredCaps` field.\n- `builtinCapability`: implementing the interface is enough; there is no `DeclaredCaps` field to check.\n- `nonDeclarerCapability`: `CapabilityDeclarer` agents are refused even if they implement the interface (`LateTranscriptWriter`, `OutOfBandTokenSource`).\n\n`nonDeclarerCapability` replaces two hand-written copies of the same logic. Five existing helpers moved onto the standard functions without changing their signatures, and five new helpers replace direct type assertions: `AsSkillDiscoverer`, `AsRestoredSessionPathResolver`, `AsProtectedFilesProvider`, `AsHookConfigLocator`, and `AsSessionFileCandidatesProvider`.\n\n## Guards\n\n- An AST test checks that every `As*` helper uses one of the three functions, that the list above `DeclaredCaps` (now 27 entries) exactly matches the `builtinCapability` and `nonDeclarerCapability` helpers, that it is sorted, and that the entries marked `(refuses CapabilityDeclarer agents)` are exactly the `nonDeclarerCapability` helpers.\n- A `testutil.GitGrepGuard` test fails on any type assertion or type-switch case that names a capability interface from package `agent`, so callers have to go through the helper and its declaration check. `Agent`, `CapabilityDeclarer`, `SessionLocator`, and `TestOnly` are allowed, each with a stated reason.\n\n## Behavior change\n\nRestoring a session (`manual_commit_pending.go`) previously type-asserted the agent to `PromptExtractor` directly. External agents always implement `ExtractPrompts`, so an external agent that declared `transcript_analyzer: false` still had its prompts extracted for the restore preview, which also ran its `extract-prompts` subcommand. It now goes through `AsPromptExtractor` and respects the declaration. This bug predates this PR. ---- MuskanPaliwal 2026-08-24T12:51:59Z
Hi @Soph , this pr addresses #1877 out-of-scope documentation fix. Would appreciate your review on this. Thanks!
---- Soph 2026-08-31T16:36:13Z
Verified every entry against the source - an `As*` helper in `capabilities.go` is ungated exactly when it resolves by bare type assertion rather than `declaredCapability[T]`, which is 10 helpers. The list goes from 5/10 to 9/10 with this change, and all four additions are correct. `SessionEndBudgeter` wasn't in the review note you cited, so that one's a genuine find on top of the ask (the PR body says "three interfaces" but the diff adds four - worth reconciling).

**One still missing: `ToolInvocationScanner`** (`capabilities.go:230`). It belongs between `SkillEventExtractor` and `SessionEndBudgeter`, which is exactly where the gap is in declaration order.

Not really your miss, though: `AsToolInvocationScanner` landed on 2026-08-24 in `a1dd3efc3`, after this PR was opened but before it merged main on the 26th. The list went stale again inside the lifetime of the fix for staleness.

Which is the more useful thing here. This list is hand-maintained with no sync mechanism and has now rotted twice, and all 10 ungated helpers already carry their own, more detailed rationale next to the code - `AsHookFreshness` explains the template-based drift, `AsSessionEndBudgeter` explains the parse-hook split. The aggregate list duplicates information that already lives at the definition, which is why it rots.

Two ways to make this the last fix needed:

1. **Stop enumerating.** Replace the parenthetical with a pointer: "...are intentionally excluded - their `As*` helpers resolve by type assertion alone (`builtinCapability`), each documenting its own reason at the helper." Nothing lost, drift surface gone.
2. **Make it testable.** A `go/ast` test over `capabilities.go` classifying each `func As*` by whether it calls `declaredCapability`, asserting the ungated set matches the names in the doc comment. ~40 lines, fails the moment capability #11 lands.

Happy to take either, or just the one-word addition if you'd rather keep it simple.

---- MuskanPaliwal 2026-08-31T20:06:39Z
Thanks @Soph, good catch. I went with the AST-backed option.

The follow-up commit makes every package-level `As*` helper use either `builtinCapability` or `declaredCapability`. The test scans production files across the top-level `agent` package, so it catches helpers outside `capabilities.go`, including `AsContextInjector` and `AsModelLister`. It derives the built-in set from those helpers and checks that the `DeclaredCaps` list matches it exactly and stays alphabetized.

I also added `ToolInvocationScanner` and characterization tests for the four normalized helpers. Their signatures, return values, and declaration behavior are unchanged.

The guard currently covers all 23 `As*` helpers, 13 built-in and 10 declaration-gated, without hard-coding those counts. `mise run check` passes. I also removed `ToolInvocationScanner` from the documentation temporarily and confirmed that the test failed with the expected mismatch.

I’ve updated the PR description to match the new scope.

---- MuskanPaliwal 2026-10-13T13:17:21Z
Thanks for the second pass, @Soph. You were right on all four, and this push fixes each one.

1. The guard only looked at `As*` helpers, so five capabilities that callers type-asserted directly slipped past it: `SkillDiscoverer`, `RestoredSessionPathResolver`, `ProtectedFilesProvider`, `HookConfigLocator` and `SessionFileCandidatesProvider`. Each one has a helper now. A new `testutil.GitGrepGuard` test fails on any type assertion or type-switch case that names a capability interface. I left `SessionLocator` and `TestOnly` out on purpose, since neither is an optional capability, and the test says why. `FileWatcher` has no production use, so it doesn't get a helper. The documented list is up to 27 entries.

2. The restore path asserted `PromptExtractor` directly, so an external agent with `transcript_analyzer: false` still had its prompts extracted and its `extract-prompts` subcommand run. It calls `AsPromptExtractor` now. The bug is older than this PR, but the new guard trips on it, so it made sense to fix it here.

3. I renamed `builtinOnlyCapability` to `nonDeclarerCapability`. That gives "built-in only" back its old meaning across the existing comments, which is "no DeclaredCaps field" and not "refuses external agents". I also reworded `inject.go` and rewrote the `CapabilityDeclarer` doc to cover all three resolvers.

4. The doc list now marks `LateTranscriptWriter` and `OutOfBandTokenSource` with `(refuses CapabilityDeclarer agents)`, and the test checks each mark against the resolver. If someone switches either helper to `builtinCapability`, the guard fails. Before, only the unit test would have caught it.

This touches files outside `agent/` too. Seven type assertions moved onto helpers, each a one-line change:

| File | Before | After | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strategy/manual_commit_pending.go`, restore preview | `.(agent.PromptExtractor)` | `agent.AsPromptExtractor` | Changed, see 2 |
| `strategy/manual_commit_pending.go`, restore path | `.(agent.RestoredSessionPathResolver)` | `agent.AsRestoredSessionPathResolver` | Same |
| `review/picker.go`, 2 sites | `.(agent.SkillDiscoverer)` | `agent.AsSkillDiscoverer` | Same |
| `agent/registry.go` | `.(HookConfigLocator)`, `.(ProtectedFilesProvider)` | `AsHookConfigLocator`, `AsProtectedFilesProvider` | Same |
| `agent/session_store.go` | `.(SessionFileCandidatesProvider)` | `AsSessionFileCandidatesProvider` | Same |

The six unchanged sites use `builtinCapability`, which returns exactly what the old assertion did, external agents included. That matters for `AllProtectedFiles`, because the external adapter forwards `ProtectedFiles` from the agent's info response and that still gets collected. One small signature change: the store holds a `SessionLocator`, not an `Agent`, so `builtinCapability` takes `any` now. It's unexported, so nothing outside the package sees it.

I wrote the tests first and watched them fail on the old code. The guard flagged exactly the seven assertions, and the restore test reproduced the prompt extraction. Then I broke each guard on purpose to check it catches the problem. `mise run check` passes, and the PR description is updated.

Would appreciate another look when you get a chance.

**They all go through `testutil.GitGrepGuard`, which owns three flags.** Each was
missing from at least one guard, and the same one was missing from three:

- `--untracked`. `git grep` searches the INDEX. Every one of these guards has
  "someone just added a file" as its subject, so the file it most needs to see is
  the one not yet staged. Two failure shapes were worse than a miss: the
  hook-config guard compares two sets built from the same blind grep, so a new
  agent package calling `OpenHookConfig` without declaring `HookConfigRelPath`
  was absent from both and the comparison *passed*; and the root-base guard's
  staleness half reported a just-added entry as STALE, telling the author to
  delete the entry that legitimised their new root.
- `--no-color`. `color.ui`/`color.grep` set to `always` colorizes into a pipe and
  the escapes land in the **filename** field. True of `-l` too, which looks
  immune. Guards then either misparse (read as staleness, #2248) or compare
  garbage to garbage while their "did we match anything" assertion still passes.
- Repo-selector scrubbing. Git exports `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` to hooks and
  they outrank `cmd.Dir`, so a `go test` under a hook or `git rebase --exec`
  scanned a different repository. `RunGit`'s isolation does **not** cover this:
  it filters `GIT_CONFIG_*` only.

Two rules for writing one:

- **A pathspec restricted to `*.go`, so an unparseable path can be fatal.** The
  `git status` guard passed a bare `cmd internal`, which also matched testdata
  `.jsonl` and a `.md`, so its non-`.go` branch had to `continue` — and that
  skip was the only thing between colorized output and a guard that silently
  checked nothing.
- **Fail on zero matches.** A detection pattern that goes stale otherwise passes
  forever. `GitGrepGuard` does this itself; the `checked == 0` tallies are the
  second half of the same idea.

### Code Duplication Prevention

Before implementing Go code, search nearby packages and utilities for reusable patterns. Use `/go:discover-related` when available; otherwise use `rg` and inspect related implementations and tests.

**Check for duplication:**

```bash
mise run dup           # Comprehensive check (threshold 50) with summary
mise run dup:staged    # Check only staged files
mise run lint          # Normal lint includes dupl at threshold 75 (new issues only)
mise run lint:full     # All issues at threshold 75
	return "", nil
}

// must still exclude it — verifies the built-in-only gate).

}

content.text:
I re-reviewed PR #2028 at the current head (`4aa3d11ae`) and found nothing blocking. The code does what the description says. I found one documentation gap worth fixing before Soph looks at it again, plus a few small cleanups.

**Verified**
- The `agent`, `strategy` and `review` package tests pass locally, including the three new guard tests (`TestCapabilityHelpersUseStandardResolver`, `TestDeclaredCapsBuiltinListMatchesCapabilityHelpers`, `TestCapabilitiesAreOnlyReachedThroughHelpers`).
- On CI, lint, canary, windows and codex-hooks pass. `test-core` and the three `test-integration` jobs were still pending when I checked.
- `builtinCapability` now takes a `SessionLocator` instead of an `Agent`. That's safe: `Agent` has every method `SessionLocator` needs, and a nil `Agent` still becomes a nil locator, so the nil check still works.
- The only behavior change is `restoredPromptPreview`, which now goes through `AsPromptExtractor`. That matches the description, and the new test covers both the declared and undeclared cases.

**Should fix**
1. **The PR description and the testing doc both claim the guard uses `GitGrepGuard`, and it doesn't.** Commit `64d225cca` switched it to parsing files with `git ls-files` plus Go's parser. The PR body still says "A `testutil.GitGrepGuard` test fails on…". `docs/development/testing.md:249` says "They all go through `testutil.GitGrepGuard`", and the repo's CLAUDE.md says the same. A reviewer will catch that mismatch. Two fixes:
   - Update the PR body to describe the parser-based approach.
   - Add a line to the testing doc noting that this guard parses instead of greps, and that it rebuilds GitGrepGuard's protections on purpose: it includes untracked files (`--others`), uses `GuardGitEnv()`, restricts to `*.go`, and fails when it checks nothing.

**Nits**
2. **A file the guard can't read is skipped, not failed** (`capability_assertion_guard_test.go:694`). It only logs and moves on. That's right for a file deleted from the worktree but still in git's index. But `GuardGitEnv` drops the user's git config, so git's default quoting of non-ASCII paths applies, and such a path would fail to open and be skipped without failing the test. No Go file in the repo has a non-ASCII path today. Passing `-z` to `git ls-files` would remove the risk.
3. **Two test comments use the old wording** (`capabilities_test.go:99,108`). They say "verifies the built-in-only gate", which describes the refuse-declarers behavior. The PR now uses "built-in only" to mean "no DeclaredCaps field", so these should say something like "verifies the nonDeclarerCapability refusal".
4. **The two capability-helper guard tests don't check the declared field.** The resolver test confirms a helper calls `declaredCapability` but not which `DeclaredCaps` field it checks, so a helper that checks the wrong field would still pass. That's outside this PR's scope and I wouldn't add it here.

Once CI is green, check the trail's findings as the repo's CLAUDE.md requires after a push. I can draft the updated PR description and the testing-doc paragraph for you to approve if you'd like.
